newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Kansas harvest set to resume.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Kansas harvest set to resume.

text.p: Harvesting of hard red winter wheat looked set to resume Friday afternoon across much of Kansas, grain dealers said.
Many harvest areas were drying out after heavy rains swept through the state Wednesday night.
"Last night was the first night all week that we didn't have any rain, so today will be the first full day in fields for some (producers)," a south central Kansas dealer said.
"Of course, there are places out west and north that got too much rain (Wednseday night), so they won't get in until late afternoon or possibly tomorrow," the dealer said.
"It was dry all night in the western two-thirds of Kansas," said Jeff Penner, meteorolgist with the Weather Center Co in Kansas City.
Penner said the only rain that fell overnight was south and east of Emporia, Kansas -- an area that typically does not produce much wheat.
Dealers said movement was slow Thursday, and basis bids were mostly unchanged.
